analysis.body:
# Grid Interconnection Snapshot for AI Data Center Observers

The five major US grid operators are tracking approximately 1.46 million MW of generation and storage projects in their queues as of mid-September 2026. ERCOT alone holds 438,086 MW across 1,778 requests, while MISO manages the largest request volume with 3,846 projects totaling 299,720 MW. This queue depth reflects multi-year backlogs for all types of generation. Battery storage—critical for data center power reliability—accounts for 326,700 MW across ERCOT, MISO, and SPP combined, though California's queue is notably storage-heavy at 46,940 MW of its 71,678 MW total. Gas-fired capacity in the queues sits at 185,544 MW across all operators, substantially larger than solar's 268,760 MW, suggesting the grid is building flexibility to match variable loads and renewable generation profiles.

Commercial sector electricity sales across eight major states reached 54,797 MWh in June 2026, with Texas leading at 15,753 MWh and California second at 10,024 MWh. Pricing varies dramatically by region, from $8.66 per MWh in Texas to $27.33 in California—a three-fold spread that reflects both local generation costs and transmission constraints. Since data centers are billed primarily as commercial customers, these state-level figures serve as rough proxies for their load footprints, though they include all non-industrial business consumption. Texas's combination of massive queue capacity and lowest-cost power illustrates why the state has become the primary draw for new data center investment.

The growth trajectory evident in both queue depth and the expansion of storage capacity suggests operators anticipate sustained high demand growth over the next five to ten years. Watch whether gas-to-storage ratios in the interconnection queues shift notably at the next reporting cycle, as accelerating storage deployment relative to new gas capacity would signal grid operators' confidence in managing data center peak loads without continuous fossil fuel reliance.
